Projects

01 / Light-Seeking Turret

Working

A servo-mounted turret sweeps a room with a light-dependent resistor, detects the brightest source against a calibrated baseline, and locks on — laser and buzzer confirming the fix.

demo — sweep, detect, lock on
  1. Calibrate — average several LDR readings with no torch present, to set a room-light baseline.
  2. Scan — sweep the servo in fixed steps, sampling the LDR at each angle.
  3. Detect — flag a reading that clears the baseline by a set margin (brighter reads smaller, on this LDR's wiring).
  4. Lock on — hold that angle, fire the laser, chirp the buzzer, hold until reset.
MCUArduino Uno R3
ActuatorSG90-class servo, pan axis
SensorLDR, voltage divider → A0
OutputLaser diode module + buzzer
On the code: first drafted with AI assistance, then bench-tested and reviewed line-by-line against this LDR and laser module's actual behaviour — not treated as finished until it was understood.

02 / Light-Following Car

In progress

Two driven wheels steer toward the brightest of a left/right LDR pair — the same sense-then-close-the-loop pattern as the turret, applied to differential drive instead of a pan axis.

  • ✓Chassis designed and 3D-printed (Bambu Lab A1)
  • ✓One DRV8833 channel bench-tested — forward / stop / reverse at safe PWM
  • !Blocked: second DRV8833 needs headers soldered before both channels can be wired
  • ·Not started: dual-LDR differential steering logic
Drivers2× DRV8833 dual motor driver
Motors2× N20 micro gear motor w/ encoder, 6 V, printed hubs
PowerBuck converter + 6×AA pack
Sensors2× LDR (left/right)
motor bring-up test · project readme
